title: Rockstar HR Manager Testifies in GTA6 Developer Union Trial
description: As the Rockstar union-busting trial heats up, an HR manager claims he had little interest in unionization evidence sent by an anonymous employee prior to layoffs.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Rockstar HR Manager Testifies in Ongoing Union Trial

As anticipation continues to build for the eventual release of *GTA6*, developer Rockstar Games finds itself embroiled in a significant legal battle. According to reports from media outlet Eurogamer, the ongoing *Rockstar Games vs Garland & Others* case is shedding light on the studio's internal labor practices, specifically regarding allegations of union-busting.

In the latest court proceedings, a Rockstar HR manager took the stand as a witness. During his testimony, he stated that he had "little interest" in evidence of unionization efforts that had been sent to him by an anonymous employee. This piece of evidence reportedly reached management prior to a substantial number of union Discord members being laid off by the developer.

## The Lead-Up to Major Layoffs

The timeline of events has become a central focus of the legal dispute. Following the receipt of the anonymous unionization materials, Rockstar proceeded with cutting a significant portion of its workforce, which notably included developers who were active members of union Discord channels. This sequence of events prompted the affected employees to take legal action, accusing the studio of targeting unionized staff.

While the HR manager's testimony attempts to distance management from active tracking of union efforts, legal representatives for the plaintiffs are scrutinizing how much the leadership knew and when they knew it. For a studio heavily reliant on stable team dynamics to finish a monumental project like *GTA6*, navigating such high-profile labor disputes is undoubtedly a delicate challenge.

## Potential Industry Implications

Labor relations within the video game industry have faced unprecedented scrutiny over recent years, with more developers pushing for union representation to secure better working conditions and job security. While there is no official indication from the source material that this trial will disrupt the production timeline of *GTA6*, the outcome of the lawsuit could set a notable precedent for how major publishers handle internal organization efforts moving forward.

## Editor's Take

This trial highlights the growing tension between major gaming corporations and the rising wave of industry unionization. Whether the HR manager's claim of having "little interest" in union efforts holds weight in court remains to be seen. Regardless of the legal outcome, it's a stark reminder that the human cost and labor politics behind 3A development are just as complex as the technology powering games like *GTA6*.
